evidence.finding: Native-dtype arithmetic candidate scored geo_mean 0.915038 (below the 0.9625098543 unchanged starting point). Worst cases: bf16 16M 0.637x, fp16 16M 0.803x; fp32 16M 0.931x; small fp16 1024/65536 0.915/0.898x. All three large-input losses concentrate around the 16M dtype paths, i.e. the changed multiply dtype.

The prior delivered candidate (measured 0.9625098543x starting point) computes y=(x.to(tl.float32)*57.29577951308232).to(x.dtype) in BOTH kernels. Its host run/_install/_launch_strided path is otherwise byte-identical to the regressed candidate, so the 0.9625->0.915 drop is attributable to the arithmetic-dtype change alone, not to host or launch code.

Transferred host-side method: on the contiguous hot path query immutable launch metadata from a plan cache and avoid repeated bookkeeping; keep device/dtype/numel/alignment/scalar keys and dynamically read current pointer and stream; never cache tensor, pointer or stream values; preserve non-contiguous/unaligned/tail fallbacks.

hypothesis: Materialising the reciprocal constant in the input dtype makes 16-bit tiles run a native bf16/fp16 multiply, which the Ascend vector pipeline executes far slower than an fp32 multiply with explicit up/down converts (bf16 16M fell to 0.637x). Restoring the fp32 multiply-and-cast semantics returns to the 0.9625x starting arithmetic. Beyond that, the remaining fixed per-call cost on small inputs is generic host bookkeeping in run(): two separate size-class dictionaries plus branch-based block/key selection. Consolidating them into one immutable plan cache (launch handle, function, packed metadata, block, keyed by device/dtype/alignment/scalar/size-class) and binding hot-path lookups as local defaults removes a dict-selection branch and repeated global lookups, without caching tensor, pointer or stream, and without removing device/alignment/scalar-specialization correctness.
change: 1) Restore y=(x.to(tl.float32)*57.29577951308232).to(x.dtype) in both _rad2deg_contig_kernel and _rad2deg_strided_kernel (original precision semantics). 2) Replace the two size-class dicts with one plan cache keyed by (device, dtype, ptr&15, n==1, size_class) storing (launch, function, packed_metadata, block); compute grid once; bind _plans/_plans.get/_get_stream as default-arg locals on run to cut per-call global lookups. Keep max-i32 path, strided/tail branches, dynamic pointer and stream queries, and cold compile-then-execute-once.
expected: Restoring fp32 multiply-and-cast recovers the fp16/bf16 16M cases toward starting-point levels (the 0.9625x baseline). The consolidated plan cache trims a small, fixed sub-microsecond host cost per call, mainly benefiting the 1024/65536 cases; geometric mean should exceed the measured 0.9625098543x starting point. Reaching a full 1.0x CANN still depends on 16-bit conversion throughput and fp32 16M bandwidth and is not guaranteed.
validation: Run preflight on the edited candidate; then the full 36-case KGS contract plus 42/42 supplementary checks on the same source; read the per-case performance feedback (especially fp16/bf16/fp32 16M and the two smallest sizes) and compare geo_mean against 0.9625098543x.
alternatives: Attribute the regression to host launch bookkeeping: rejected because starter.py and candidate.py share an identical host path and differ only in the two kernel arithmetic lines.
Keep the native-dtype multiply but change block size: rejected because the per-dtype 16M losses track the multiply dtype, not tiling, and this would repeat the disallowed low-precision mechanism.
discriminating_observation: Host code is identical between the 0.9625x starter and the 0.9150x candidate (single diff in each kernel's arithmetic); therefore the large-input regression must originate in the changed dtype of the multiply, and restoring it is a precondition rather than a new optimization.
